hooks.text: A crashed space probe fell silent, yet spoke from Venus weeks later.
How did a broken Soviet lander transmit data from Venus in secret?
Twenty-three minutes of hidden data proved Venus was a scorching furnace.

title: The Silent Lander That Spoke From Venus
description: Discover how a damaged Soviet probe transmitted history-making data from the surface of Venus.

beats.text: A crashed space probe fell silent, yet spoke from Venus weeks later.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Venera lander on the Venusian surface, 1970

beats.text: On December 15, 1970, the Soviet Union's Venera 7 reached the dark night side of Venus.
beats.visual: Diagram of the Venusian atmosphere layers, 1970

beats.text: Engineers built the lander with a titanium pressure shell and chilled its interior to survive the extreme environment.
beats.visual: The titanium pressure vessel during fabrication, 1970

beats.text: But during descent, the parachute failed, causing the probe to strike the surface at seventeen meters per second.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the probe falling through thick orange clouds, 1970

beats.text: Mission controllers initially believed the spacecraft died instantly when it fell completely silent on impact.
beats.visual: Illustration of the probe lying on its side in the dark, 1970

beats.text: Weeks later, scientists reviewing recorded radio tapes discovered a faint, twenty-three minute signal hidden beneath the static.
beats.visual: Soviet radio astronomer Oleg Rzhiga or similar equipment, 1970

beats.text: The transmissions confirmed a crushing pressure ninety times that of Earth and a temperature of four hundred seventy-five degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the exoplanet or Venusian surface, 1970

beats.text: Those faint tapes proved that the silent spacecraft had actually survived to make history.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Venera lander on the Venusian surface, 1970

better_than_last: This version applies reviewer feedback on Beat 8 to start with 'Those faint tapes proved that' while expanding the word count to exactly 130 words to meet the target duration of 45-50 seconds.
